# Cardano interoperability fixture

`conway-v11.block` is copied unchanged from the Pallas project's real mainnet
Conway fixture. It is lowercase hex of the complete block with its era wrapper.
`conway-v11-upstream.md` is the unchanged upstream record asserting the network,
slot, block hash and protocol version. The full Apache 2.0 license is retained
as `LICENSE.pallas`.

Pinned source: [txpipe/pallas at daecef59a1979d89515524d9583cc28655af182c](https://github.com/txpipe/pallas/tree/daecef59a1979d89515524d9583cc28655af182c).

Original files:

- [test_data/conway-v11.block](https://github.com/txpipe/pallas/blob/daecef59a1979d89515524d9583cc28655af182c/test_data/conway-v11.block)
- [test_data/conway-v11.md](https://github.com/txpipe/pallas/blob/daecef59a1979d89515524d9583cc28655af182c/test_data/conway-v11.md)
- [LICENSE](https://github.com/txpipe/pallas/blob/daecef59a1979d89515524d9583cc28655af182c/LICENSE)

`conway-v11.json` contains Syn's fixture checksums and extraction metadata. The
block hash, slot and protocol version come from the upstream record. The block
number, previous hash and header offsets were decoded independently with cbor2
and checked against the raw header's Blake2b-256 digest. These values were not
generated by Syn's Cardano implementation. For this exact fixture the 860-byte
header starts at byte 3; this is fixture metadata, not a general CBOR parser.

Chain-sync uses era tag 6 for Conway headers; the complete block wrapper uses
tag 7 because it counts Byron epoch-boundary and regular blocks separately.
See the pinned [Pallas header decoder](https://github.com/txpipe/pallas/blob/daecef59a1979d89515524d9583cc28655af182c/pallas-traverse/src/header.rs).
